1.title: Core Infrastructure Security in Azure
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Core Infrastructure Security in Azure. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft security solutions. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Describe Azure D dos (distributed denial of service) Protection. Describe Azure Firewall. Describe Azure Web Application Firewall (waff). Describe network segmentation with Azure virtual networks. Describe network security groups (N S Gs). Describe Azure Bastion. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft security solutions (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: Seven services at a glance
1.text: Seven services at a glance. Azure D dos Protection. Job in one line: Defends against flood attacks that try to make a service unavailable. Works at: Layers three and four. Azure Firewall. Job in one line: Managed, cloud-native firewall that filters traffic for virtual networks. Works at: Layers three to seven (network and application rules). Azure Web Application Firewall (waff). Job in one line: Protects web applications from common web attacks. Works at: Layer seven (H T T P). Virtual networks and subnets. Job in one line: Segment resources into isolated networks. Works at: Network design.

1.title: Seven services at a glance, continued
1.text: Seven services at a glance. Network security groups (N S Gs). Job in one line: Allow or deny traffic to and from resources by rules. Works at: Layers three and four. Azure Bastion. Job in one line: Secure R D P and S S H to V Ms without exposing public I P addresses. Works at: Access. Azure Key Vault. Job in one line: Store and control secrets, keys and certificates. Works at: Data and secrets.

1.title: Seven services at a glance, continued
1.text: Seven services at a glance. The figure shows this: Where each Azure security service sits: internet edge, application, network, virtual machines and secrets.

1.title: Azure DDoS Protection
1.text: Azure D dos Protection. A distributed denial-of-service (D dos) attack floods a target with traffic so real users cannot reach it. Infrastructure protection. Default protection included for Azure services at no extra charge. D dos Network Protection and I P Protection. Paid tiers with adaptive tuning to your traffic, attack analytics and metrics, alerts, and rapid response support. Layers. Defends network (layer three) and transport (layer four) attacks. Exam tip: D dos equals availability attack, many sources, volume. D dos Protection handles layers three and four; the waff handles layer seven web attacks.

1.title: Azure Firewall
1.text: Azure Firewall. Azure Firewall is a managed, cloud-based, stateful network security service with built-in high availability and unlimited scaling. Network and application rules. Filter by I P, port and protocol, and by F Q D N (website names). Threat intelligence filtering. Alert or block traffic to and from known malicious I P addresses and domains. nat rules (D N A T). Publish an internal service through the firewall. Tiers. Basic, Standard and Premium (Premium adds T L S inspection and intrusion detection and prevention). Central management. One policy for many networks and subscriptions. Exam tip: Azure Firewall equals central, managed firewall for network traffic (including F Q D N filtering). An N S G is simpler, per subnet or N I C. The waff is only for web applications.

1.title: Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF)
1.text: Azure Web Application Firewall (waff). The waff protects web applications against common exploits and vulnerabilities such as sequel injection and cross-site scripting, using oh wasp rule sets. It inspects H T T P and H T T P S (layer seven) requests. It runs on Azure Application Gateway, Azure Front Door and Azure C D N.

1.title: Network segmentation and NSGs
1.text: Network segmentation and N S Gs. Segmentation splits a network into smaller, isolated parts so a breach cannot spread easily. Azure virtual network (V net). A private, isolated network in Azure. Subnets. Segments of a V net for tiers such as web, app and data. V net peering. Connects virtual networks privately. Network security group. Filters traffic between subnets and to or from the internet.

1.title: How an NSG works
1.text: How an N S G works. An N S G contains security rules. Each rule has priority, source, destination, port, protocol and action (allow or deny). Rules are processed from the lowest priority number first; the first match wins. N S Gs are stateful and can be applied to a subnet or a network interface.

1.title: How an NSG works, continued
1.text: How an N S G works. The figure shows this: An N S G rule table: priority, source, destination, port, protocol and action. Exam tip: N S G equals allow or deny by rule (five-tuple: source, destination, port, protocol, plus priority). Lowest number is checked first. Subnets plus N S Gs are the basic way to segment an Azure network.

1.title: Azure Bastion
1.text: Azure Bastion. Azure Bastion is a fully managed service that gives secure R D P and S S H access to virtual machines directly in the Azure portal over T L S, without a public I P address on the V M and without opening R D P or S S H ports to the internet.

1.title: Azure Bastion, continued
1.text: Azure Bastion. No public I P on the V M. Shrinks the attack surface. Protection from port scanning. R D P and S S H ports are not exposed. Browser-based. Connect from the portal, no client software.

1.title: Azure Key Vault
1.text: Azure Key Vault. Key Vault is a secure store for secrets (passwords, connection strings, A P I keys), keys (encryption keys) and certificates. Centralized secret management. No secrets in code or config files. Access control. By Azure R B A C (or access policies) and managed identities. H S M-backed keys. Hardware security module protection (Premium tier). Logging. Audit who accessed what. Certificate lifecycle. Request, store and renew certificates. Exam tip: "Store secrets, keys and certificates securely and keep passwords out of code" equals Key Vault. Apps reach it with a managed identity.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors needs to connect to a V M over R D P without giving the V M a public I P address or opening R D P to the internet. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Bastion. Bastion provides R D P and S S H through the portal over T L S without exposing public I P s.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A web shop wants protection against sequel injection and cross-site scripting. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Web Application Firewall. The waff protects web applications from common layer seven attacks.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which service helps keep a site available during a large flood of traffic from many sources? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure D dos Protection. D dos Protection defends against volumetric attacks at layers three and four.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team needs to store database passwords and encryption keys so that they are not in application code. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure Key Vault. Key Vault stores secrets, keys and certificates securely.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which control allows or denies traffic to a subnet based on source, destination, port, protocol and priority? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A network security group. N S Gs filter traffic with prioritized allow and deny rules.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company wants one managed service with F Q D N filtering and threat intelligence for traffic across several virtual networks. Which fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Firewall. Azure Firewall is a managed central firewall with F Q D N filtering and threat intelligence.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which layers does Azure D dos Protection defend? Answer: Layers three and four (network and transport). Question two. What does the waff protect? Answer: Web applications from attacks such as sequel injection and cross-site scripting. Question three. What is an N S G? Answer: A set of allow and deny rules for network traffic.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does Azure Bastion avoid? Answer: Public I P addresses and open R D P or S S H ports on V Ms. Question five. What three things does Key Vault store? Answer: Secrets, keys and certificates. Question six. How do N S G rules get processed? Answer: By priority, lowest number first, first match wins.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. D dos Protection: floods; layers three and four; default infrastructure protection, paid Network or I P Protection. Azure Firewall: managed central firewall; network and application rules, F Q D N, threat intelligence. waff: layer seven web attacks (sequel injection, X S S); on Application Gateway, Front Door, C D N. V net, subnets, N S Gs: segmentation; N S G rules by priority, source, destination, port, protocol, action. Bastion and Key Vault: R D P and S S H without public I P; secrets, keys, certificates, H S M-backed, managed identities. In the next module, we continue the course.
